title: OpenAI and AMD Show How AI Can Accelerate Chip Design
gist: OpenAI says its models rewrote SystemVerilog to improve PPA of circuitry in AMD's flagship GPU by up to 14% versus already heavily optimized baselines, with some changes reaching a taped-out design, plus single-digit gains in AMD's upcoming flagship CPU and ~10% matrix-unit area reduction in OpenAI's Broadcom-built Jalapeño inference chip. Synopsys tools verified the results, pointing to AI expanding design-space exploration within fixed schedules.

insights.claim: OpenAI models improved the power, performance and area (PPA) of circuitry in AMD's flagship GPU by up to 14% against baselines engineers had already heavily optimized.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: AI-optimized RTL could become a competitive PPA lever for chip designers like AMD.
insights.quote: by up to 14% against baselines that engineers had already heavily optimized
insights.locator: OpenAI says its models helped improve

insights.claim: OpenAI describes the AMD chip-design work as roughly a year's worth of engineering progress in under five months.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Implies large compression of chip design cycles if repeatable.
insights.quote: roughly a year’s worth of engineering progress in under five months
insights.locator: OpenAI says its models helped improve

insights.claim: Some OpenAI model-generated improvements made it into an AMD design recently released for manufacturing (tape-out), per Greg Brockman, and AMD added other changes to production design files for future versions.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Moves AI chip design from research to production silicon; a real adoption milestone.
insights.locator: OpenAI says its models helped improve

insights.claim: AMD verified single-digit percentage PPA gains in key blocks of its upcoming flagship CPU using model-written designs, suggesting AI-assisted optimization helps across several kinds of circuitry.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Gains are smaller on CPU than GPU; generality across block types matters for adoption.

insights.claim: AMD Chair and CEO Lisa Su publicly welcomed the OpenAI chip-design results on X, saying she was proud of the work.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: CEO-level endorsement suggests AMD will keep deepening the OpenAI design collaboration.

insights.claim: OpenAI's models rewrote SystemVerilog code governing calculation, control operations and data movement, while Synopsys design tools verified behavior and measured power, speed and area trade-offs.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: LLMs augment rather than replace EDA: verification tools like Synopsys remain the trust layer, supporting EDA incumbents.

insights.claim: AI-assisted design lets chip designers test more promising ideas within a fixed schedule, turning circuit improvements that once took weeks of manual iteration into options explored alongside several alternatives.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Broader design-space exploration could raise PPA across the industry and increase EDA compute/verification demand.
insights.quote: A circuit improvement that once demanded weeks of manual iteration could become practical to explore alongside several alternatives.
insights.locator: The opportunity is to give chip designers

insights.claim: OpenAI validated Jalapeño, its first custom inference chip developed with Broadcom, in physical silicon and estimates model-proposed changes cut the standard-cell area of its matrix unit by about 10%.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: OpenAI's in-house silicon with Broadcom is real and using its own models to optimize; relevant to Broadcom custom-ASIC and Nvidia displacement narratives.
